utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-08-91-T. The Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances for today, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner assisted by Jasmina Bosnjakovic for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Appearing for Mr. Stanisic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Tatjana Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence appearing, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While the witness is being escorted back to the stand by the usher, we would wish to alert the parties that, for reasons which I needn't go into, when we take the adjournment today, will resume at 2.15 not 10.00 tomorrow morning. Not -- 9.00 tomorrow morning, I should have said. We would be swapping places with the Gotovina trial which was scheduled to resume in the afternoon, and they are taking the morning slot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Borovcanin. Before I invite Mr. Cvijetic to continue -- to resume his cross-examination, I remind you you are still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I begin, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Before we begin, I'd like to take you back to a document that Ms. Korner showed you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up 65 ter 2398.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, in your binder it's tab 38. Have you got it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now we have to wait for the Trial Chamber to see it. Yesterday you discussed the first page of this document with Ms. Korner regarding the engagement of policemen from Bratunac and Skelani stations in combat operations, and you dwelled on the penultimate paragraph which concerns the engagement of police in the so-called mopping up. Do you remember the questions the Trial Chamber and the Prosecutor asked you about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to page 3 in B/C/S and Tatjana will maybe help us find the reference in English. It's page 3 in English too.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: There's this paragraph which begins with the words "at the station of Skelani a special unit was formed under the command of Dusko Mandic." So when you arrived at Skelani, you found one of those ad hoc "special units" including about 20 personnel, and you said, in fact, the document says the unit was engaged under the local military command in mopping up. You will agree that this sentence clarifies what you said yesterday, even in these operations, this unit was resubordinated to the military command and followed their orders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the military were always on the ground, and it was not possible to work in circumvention of the military command.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This was a case of mopping up the remaining enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph, you as an inspector point out that this special unit has no legal grounds for its existence, and in keeping with the minister's orders, it has to be disbanded and placed at the disposal of the Army of Republika Srpska, and part of its men should be used to reinforce that police detachment pursuant to the law?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What struck me in this report is on the previous page, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it's page 22 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This is the large paragraph which begins with the words, "from the moment it was established, the police station was engulfed in a series of problems." And you will notice your own comment in that paragraph. You say: "Pursuant to a decision of the minister of the interior, Bogdan Stevanovic was appointed commanding officer, and Milos Vasiljevic was appointed his deputy. At the same time, local municipal bodies, without the approval of the ministry, appointed Slavoljub Simic commander and Ostoja Bozic his deputy." Mr. Borovcanin, what was going on? The minister appointed the commander and deputy and the local authorities simultaneously appointed two of their men to the same posts. How did you resolve this problem eventually?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this duality could not last on the ground, and if we had left things as they were and left the local appointees in their place, then the ministry would have lost its authority. For that reason, I insisted during my visit that the minister's orders be followed and a discussion was held with these men who were appointed by the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In this case, you succeeded in handling things this way, but you will agree there were other cases where the local authorities offered much more resistance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I don't want to sound immodest, but in talking to people and presenting my arguments, I succeeded in convincing people that this was not a good way to work, and things were resolved that way. In some other places, we were not recognised as an authority at all. They understood us as something decorative, people who were just passing through, and they couldn't wait to see our backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I have another example for that, we'll come back to that later. Here on the -- in the last paragraph we have another comment you made in the paragraph that begins with the words: "Of all the employees in the Skelani Public Security Station, only four employees have letters of appointment from the Ministry of the Interior. The rest of the employees were appointed pursuant to a decision issued by the self-proclaimed commander of the Territorial Defence and now the Serbian army." This sort of confirms what you just said, a local commander in Skelani took it upon himself to fill major posts in the Skelani Police Station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. On that occasion, we reviewed things and we wanted to see letters of appointments, and we found out that only four policemen had appropriate decisions, formal decisions. And the late Marko Milanovic issued decisions for the rest of the personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The reason I wanted to deal with this issue is that it concerns the mechanism for enforcing the decisions of the ministry in situations when the local communities appointed their own commanders and deputy commanders, and that was aggravated by the fact that local authorities were providing the financing. You will agree that it was difficult to defend the ministry's authority in such situations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly was. In yesterday's evidence, I said, and I heard that myself on my field missions, the local authorities would say, If we pay for it, then we appoint these people. And they indeed did. They provided the uniforms, the equipment, and everything. But that was not a good way to work. That's no way to establish an institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We have already said that the mechanism of enforcing decisions is important, and one important factor therein is financing. The financing has to come from the budget through the ministry and then you have a better discipline?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the main principle in the functioning of any government in the world, it has to be financed from the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now, in keeping with our general discussion about the various lines of work of the ministry and the problems to which the minister had to react, I want to show you 1D99. It's your tab 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did I say 1D99? That's the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, this document is already exhibited, so we won't dwell on it long. It's an order from President Karadzic written in longhand whereby he orders Minister Stanisic to assemble 60 members of what he refers to as specially trained policemen and to resubordinate them to the military command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. These men should go to the front line in Nedjarici I chose this order to put to you because these policemen who left on these orders come originally from the area you controlled. I want to ask you if the absence of these 60 policemen affected the continued ability of your police force to carry out their regular police work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm looking at the typing on the screen in order not to start my answer too early. Certainly their absence was very strongly felt. It's not a small number of people. And now you reminded me of something else. Whenever men were absent on the front line, that would give a lot of leeway to the criminals, the local criminals, to increase their activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You gave me a cue for my next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I call for 1D100.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's your tab 12. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What you just said to the Trial Chamber is almost the same thing that Mr. Stanisic said addressing directly the Presidency. He says, We have executed your order and provided 60 employees of the MUP. And in the next paragraph he says, These men are not special policemen; they were not trained for special operations. And then read the last paragraph. He proposes that they be replaced by regular army troops so that they could continue with their regular police work. And in paragraph 2 he says why. The roads Hresa, Pale, Vogosca, and other roads are no longer covered but the police.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only confirm. These roads had become very unsafe and very risky for regular passengers, for the police, for army troops, for anyone, because they were constantly under sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I have shown these two documents just to corroborate what you said, namely, that the minister pursued these problems and tried to resolve them. Now, I'll show you 65 ter 261. It's a document that we have not exhibited so far. It's your tab 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, it has been exhibited, and it's 1D49. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Have you looked through it? You see in the first paragraph the minister orders that all active-duty police officers be withdrawn from the front line while the reserve policemen be placed on war-time assignments at the disposal of the Army of Republika Srpska. We have a different term here, not resubordination. They are to be taken off the police roster and placed at the disposal of the army. So, in October 1992, the minister suggests a final solution to this problem. In paragraph 2, he even suggests a ratio in which the forces should remain. He says, The rest of the reserve police force are to be made available for war-time assignment to the Army of Republika Srpska. And the tone is that of an ultimatum and even angry, I would say. And he says to all the heads of the centres, You must inform all military commands that it is not your duty to send policemen to the front line. Does this sound to you as if Minister Stanisic had finally lost his patience and he is offering reserve policemen to the army, while insisting that the active-duty policemen remain on the police force? Have you heard about the position he had taken in your work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly I am aware of this. But I have to add how this dispatch came to be sent. In the centre where I worked, we heard a lot of criticism from the Army of Republika Srpska over what they thought was insufficient police engagement on front lines, so this antagonism was something continuous. On the other hand, we were criticised by the local authorities: Why are you not doing more to suppress crime? So we were under fire from both sides. And that's why I believe the minister made this rather dramatic move. I mentioned this yesterday, talking about the ratio between the active-duty and reserve personnel. Before the war, it was clear 1:3 or 1:5 in certain stations, and the minister here decided that it should be 1:2, not less.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So for each active-duty policemen, for each regular policemen, two reserve policemen would go or five if they were already there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the place, but not less than 1:2 was to be the ratio.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm coming to my next topic. We'll see how the minister dealt with other problems. We'll no longer deal with the engagement of police in military operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's see 1D58.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If I may, I have a question in the second point in this document. It is said that this is in regard to the newly suggested systematisation. This is the second time I hear that term and I don't know what it means. Could the witness explain what is the systematisation about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: There was no interpretation, sir. Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every institution including the Ministry of the Interior had rules on internal organisation and the systematisation of posts containing job descriptions. And based on that, manpower levels were regulated. There were also rules as to what the proportion should be in relation to active-duty policemen. And that's probably what the ministry was referring to when he said it should be 1:2 at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, do you need any further clarification? Okay. 1D58, we'll look at that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's 14 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's an order issued by the minister, and yesterday we discussed removing from the police persons who were involved in criminal proceedings or had committed a crime. So this is an order which the minister kept repeating, and he kept insisting on it at every collegium meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This is the original text. It was later copied and retyped. So, as a professional, will you tell me is it completely clear to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no doubt about it; it's completely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Then please confirm whether my interpretation is correct or not. Policemen, while they are authorised officials and wearing uniforms, are not military conscripts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: However, if their employment in the police force ends for whatever reason and if they are of the appropriate age, that same moment they become liable to military service, and they have to report to the proper authorities at the municipality for defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the Law on All People's Defence said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior was duty-bound, when terminating the employment of a police officer, to immediately deliver his personnel file to the military authority so that he would be given his war task?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. His file had to be passed on to the military post or the military command.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. However, that disciplinary responsibility or criminal responsibility had nothing do with the fact that they were becoming liable for military service; the judicial proceedings, if any, that had been instituted would continue; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. If a crime had been committed, automatically a policeman would be suspended. His official ID and his weapons would be confiscated, especially if the crime was serious, something like murder or serious theft. That would be one line of action; disciplinary proceedings. Secondly, reports would be filed, criminal reports, with the court that had jurisdiction. So that would be done if he had committed a crime when not be resubordinated to the military. However, if he had committed a crime while he was resubordinated to the military, that would be dealt with by military security. So there was no doubt about that. But disciplinary proceedings in the police station would go ahead anyway, and this could not be prejudged. We would have to wait for the end of the proceedings in order to determine whether he could continue to be a policeman or not. So as lawyers, you will understand that no ad hoc decisions could be made but we had to wait for the proceedings to be completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I just wanted us to discuss in principle the fact that putting someone at the disposal of the military authorities had no influence on either disciplinary or criminal proceedings against a person; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And we will demonstrate that using a practical example.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 1D176, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's number 15 in your binder, Mr. Borovcanin. This is one of a series of orders issued after a meeting in Belgrade, and it's quite complex because in this order, the minister deals with almost all of the problems you and I discussed yesterday in the form of an order. In item 1, he was establishing the optimum number of members of security services, and we've already spoken about that. In item 2, he repeats the order we have just commented on and which you said he repeated over and over again. In item 3, he orders that any surplus of available individuals should be placed at the disposal of the Army of the Republika Srpska. In number 4, all special units formed during the war in areas of Security Services Centres and so on are to be immediately disbanded. And this is the order you carried out on the ground. And the minister says that the detachment, a real special detachment should be set up and that anyone who is interested could apply for it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Further, in item 5, he says that this detachment should have its forward posts. And then at number 7 on the next page --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: He deals with eliminating paramilitary formations. Let's just wait for the second page to come up. Yes. Paramilitary formations. In item 8, he orders strict compliance with the law and legality in the work of the ministry. In item 9, he deals with the duty to inform the ministry of the events, and so on and so forth. Later on, we will see some exhibits that will show what the response to these orders was on the ground, but the reason I'm showing this document is, you know about this order, about disbanding special units, you knew about it when you went to Milici and other places, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you knew about this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. As soon as we received this order, we started implementing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I will now mention a number of orders which I will not bring up on the screen because the Court has seen them more than once. Just tell us whether you know about these orders. For example, 1D56 in which the minister says that any unauthorised collection centres or camps should be reported --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm really sorry, Mr. Cvijetic, but that won't do. We'll have to see the document. We have no idea otherwise, at least I have no idea, whether you are quoting accurately or what you're quoting from.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let's have 1D56 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, it's a short order. You can read it. So the minister is drawing attention to compliance with international legislation, and I think that at all these meetings you yourself insisted on this, and as an experienced policeman you knew about this obligation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was my priority at working meetings to tell everyone that whoever was imprisoned had to be urgently reported to the International Committee of the Red Cross and that these people should be provided with clothing, medicines, and so on. I kept parroting this at whatever police station I visited.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And in the second part, the minister deals with these so-called wild or unauthorised camps and prisons and says that any such camps should be reported to the ministry; is that correct? You probably knew about this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I knew about it. It's so important that one can't possibly forget it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now let's look at 1D55.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's number 17 in your binder, I do apologise. Open it in your binder; it will be easier for you. Yesterday you and I talked about these detentions, and here the minister prescribes the conditions that had to be met for people to be detained for up to three days; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In item 2, the minister says that the security of collection centres shall be the direct responsibility of the Serbian army, and if they do not have enough men for these duties, he is again offering members of the reserve police force to be placed at the army's disposal for these tasks. So you see that there is continuity in all these efforts for people to be taken from the police roster and put at the disposal of the army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. I'm trying to understand that the army was always short of men, but we were even more short of men. And the minister wanted to put reserve officers at their disposal in order for us to deal with this problem finally, because we had nothing to do with the camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yesterday I read out to you some discussions from the meeting in Belgrade, and Mr. Dobro Planojevic joined in the discussion as did Mr. Lovro [as interpreted] Tusevljak. They spoke about documenting war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 1D84 brought up on the screen, please. It's number 19 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let's just say for the benefit of the Court that Mr. Planojevic signed his name as assistant minister for the prevention and detection of crime. So please look at the document. And somewhere around the middle he says that special attention it to be paid to uncovering perpetrators of war crimes, to documenting the criminal activities, and so on and so forth. You see this part?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And towards the end he says: "As you will run into numerous obstacles in combatting crime in war time, and will on occasion be unable to take adequate measures, in such cases, record all information in Official Notes for subsequent taking of measures, that is, criminal Prosecution." So let's dwell on this for a minute. Regardless of the difficulties, regardless of the fact that the suspect may not be available, that the accused have left the area, it was your duty do everything that fell under your line of work in these circumstances, and then you would wait for a situation to arise when it was possible to prosecute?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There would be many cases of unknown perpetrators to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Tell us what you mean.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, it would not be possible to carry on a proper on-site investigation due to combat activities, for example, but that would not relieve police officers of their responsibility to carry on an investigation as soon as it was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, yesterday I asked you whether you knew of a single instance where this procedure was not carried out and where a crime was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I'm not aware of any instance where a crime was not dealt with officially.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And before I put more documents to you, I'll show you 1D63.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, can I ask the witness whose assistant minister this is, this Mr. Planojevic is, is assistant to whom? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The MUP of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's signed assistant minister for prevention and detection of crime. Is that the in Ministry of Interior or in the Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I can assist, I think you'll find his name on the chart. If it's not there, it should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. It's Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, my microphone was not switched on, but we'll clarify this. I asked for document 1D63 to be brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's number 21 in your binder, so please open it. All the centres received a letter in which it says that after the meeting in Belgrade of the 11th of July, acting on the conclusions reached at that meeting, work should be carried out on documenting war crimes and genocide. And it says here in paragraph number 2 that this refers to all persons, regardless of who the perpetrators were, Muslims, Croats, Serbs, or others. So crimes against anyone would have to be documented, and also the victims would have to be identified and recorded. So a form was sent out, it was called RZ, I think it stands for "war crime," most probably, "ratni zlocin." And let me just ask you, did you have occasion to see a form of this kind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about it, but I didn't really fill one in myself because it's the duty of the criminal service.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But you knew about the existence of the form?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the column that says nationality or ethnicity and religion, and this is an open question, so to say, any ethnicity and any religion can be entered here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you know of this document but you yourself did not use it in your work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to avoid any dilemmas, we had collegium meetings where we were all informed of all of this, but everybody then had his own line of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we understand this, so I think we can move on. Now, we have a specific instance where a lot of what we have just been dealing with theoretically is involved; crime prevention, struggles with the local authorities, disciplinary and criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let's have 1D98 on the screen because this illustrates all of these points at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, it's number 24 in your binder. You see, the prime minister Mr. Djeric is sending directly to Mr. Cedo Kljajic, under-secretary for public security; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: He demands that major criminal scandals in Republika Srpska be investigated, including the scandal involving the factory TAS, the Sarajevo car factory in Vogosca, et cetera. You know about these?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Then we won't dwell on it. We'll just see how the minister reacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D62, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your tab 25. The government sent this out on the 25th May; and on the next day, the 26th, the minister is sending a form for creating statistics on crime incidents. And what we see filled in is just an example how to use this form. Look at page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if we have the right page in English. Maybe page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In item 2, in B/C/S it's Roman numerals, the minister says under number 5: "Describe particularly serious cases of crimes committed: Public security stations of Vogosca, car theft from the TAS factory, and Ilidza have a special obligation to provide these accounts." Do you know that this followed precisely based on the reports from your inspectors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I am aware of that. I can give you more detail if you need me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We'll do it by opening documents that deal with these scandals and see how it was dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 1398.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your tab 26. Let me just see who authored this. It's your centre, and the inspectors from your centre sent this report both to the head of the centre and the minister. It's a progress report on the execution of the minister's document orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the last page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter apologises. The microphone wasn't on. It says, in addition, Borislav Maksimovic, he, at that time, was chief of the public security station of Vogosca. The answer is, Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: On the last page, the chief of the public security station Vogosca says that almost every one of his police officers had stolen a Golf, a Volkswagon Golf vehicle, which is obvious; but they would return them if anyone ever asked them to do so. And the reason why I'm showing you this document is, it says here: The opinion prevails among the police officers, including this chief, that the staffing policies in that security station can only be laid down by the SJB chief and his own personnel, and no one from the MUP or the municipality may install people in his service. In addition, it was said at the meeting that we were now unwanted and unneeded and should have come before. And so we returned on the 12th of July, 1992. This brings us back to the problems with local authorities and people who were appointed by the local authorities; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's a problem that was very pronounced in Vogosca, more, perhaps, than in other stations. And Zvornik also had very grave problems of this nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We'll follow that through the documents to see how this settlement of accounts between the ministry and the defiant police station unfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, Your Honours, this is the first document that I'm showing and hasn't been exhibited. It's 65 ter 1398. No, it has been exhibited I'm being told. It's 1D106.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, there is another one though, if I'm not wrong, that is 65 ter 536, tab order 18, which is not exhibited yet. You showed it to the witness; do you intend to make it an exhibit? 65 ter 536. Tab 18. Does it have an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me find it. That has not been shown. I did not show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Sorry about that. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So let's move to the next document, 65 ter 3094. It's your number 25. Mr. Borovcanin, a new inspection team is going to Vogosca four days later. They review the situation to see how it was possible to steal such a great number of cars. They lined up the chief, Borislav Maksimovic, and the president of the Executive Board of Vogosca, and the government's commissioner in charge of that area, as well as the commander of the factory's security detail and the commander's deputy. You can confirm from the document that a detailed inquiry had been made. First of all, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember when my colleagues went there because it was a very big deal at the time. And there was another inspection team after them. I'll tell you about it later, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What drew my attention was the third paragraph, line 3, when a number of abuses were noted, and then it says the document -- the related documentation is with Tintor and his secretary, while most of the vehicles were given for use on the basis of orders written on scraps of paper. Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. One of those people is Mr. Tintor, mentioned here. But there are others, and I can elaborate.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Tell us who Tintor was.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was up there in the government; I don't know which exact post. But I know he was an influential man, and he had his say in everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Will it help if I tell you that he was the chairman of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, now you mention it, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And finally, your inspectors suggest measures to stop any more cars from being just driven away. You know about this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have checked, this document is not yet an exhibit, and we would like to tender it. 65 ter 3094.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be document 1D182, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think that needs to be checked, Your Honours, because I'm pretty certain I showed this document to Mr. Djeric, absolutely, and I think it was marked for identification then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If it turns out that it was, then we'll have to make the correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, maybe that relates to the next document. Can we have 1D93.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your tab 28, Mr. Borovcanin. We still have to wait for the English. Oh, it's up. Mr. Borovcanin, you mentioned seeing the documents produced by the third inspection team that had intervened. We see that the ministry is now directly involved through its administration for the suppression of crime. And on page 2 we see who signed it, and it's Mr. Goran Madjar. Did you mean this intervention directly by the ministry when you were talking about the third visit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I mentioned the third visit, I wasn't sure that somebody was there from the ministry, although I'm not doubting this document. This document is okay. Goran was there too. But I can't understand why it's not in the documents. On one occasion, eight men went; four from the crime department, four from the police; because the problems were by that time very grave and we needed the police just for security. We had reports that criminals had burst into one of my colleague's hotel rooms by night. They were armed, as I said. And it's -- he can only thank his own professional alertness and adroitness that he was not gunned down. That's why I mention this incident, to just give you an example of how difficult it was to resolve this problem with the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, on this document, can you confirm that Mr. Madjar intervened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is already an exhibit. This was on the 29th July, 1992. I'm sorry, this was an MFI'd document. I suppose that's why the Legal Officer contacted you. Perhaps -- perhaps we could tender it now, since the witness is aware of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So we lift the MFI status and exhibit it. Mr. Cvijetic, when it's -- this is -- it's 10.25, so, at a convenient point, we will take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that's your decision, we can take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As a matter of courtesy to counsel, we explain the reason for our delay in resuming. The bench was -- there were certain procedurals matters on which we were meeting. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good afternoon. The Defence would like to point to a question which had to do with your last ruling of the 23rd of February which is the subpoena for the appearance of Witness 179 and 123. Namely, it is stated in that ruling that no one but the representatives of the OTP or of the state requested to execute the subpoena and VW Unit can't contact witnesses prior to their appearance in this court. As obviously this is a template that runs like a red thread through all the decisions because I've checked all the subpoenas that have been issued in this case, and all the rulings contain that part, and our practice so far has been to get in touch with all witnesses, of course, in agreement with the OTP, and we talk to them. We were drawn attention to this fact. So I should like to ask the Trial Chamber to amend its ruling in this particular section, namely, to allow the Defence team to be in contact, establish contact, with these witnesses under specific conditions and in agreement with the OTP. We talked to the Prosecutor, and I believe that the Prosecutor shall have no objection to this request of ours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, unless my fellow judges have a contrary view in which case I would reverse what -- amend what I'm about to say, it seems to me that without formally amending the order that we would have made, that the practical solution to the valid issue that you raise would be and could be resolved by the ordinary co-operation which the Chamber presumes to continually exist between counsel for the Defence and the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to say that this was raised with me in the adjournment, and I pointed out to the Defence counsel that the rule that there is no property in a witness must apply. I think the difficulty is, and it's fair to say, until this problem about witnesses arose a couple of days ago, we hadn't actually picked up the order that was contained in the summonses that the Defence shouldn't speak to them, and we've been allowing them to speak to them. But technically, I think Mr. Krgovic is right; it's a breach of Your Honours' order. We are perfectly happy, subject to what Mr. Krgovic says, that arrangements are made through us and at the witness's consent for the Defence to continue to meet with witnesses, even those who are summonsed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I fully support the observations made by the presiding judge, and so the procedure for you, Mr. Krgovic, is to address yourself to the Prosecution and ask that arrangements be made for you to meet the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Can we now see 1446, according to the 65 ter list, please. Just a minute. I do not think that this is the right document, the one which is on the screen. It is 1446 is the number. Please turn to page 2 because this is a blank page, so the next page, please, in the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, in your document it is 29, in your binder. This is eight days after Mr. Madjar, on behalf of the administration for crime prevention, dispatched this letter. This is a reminder by him for action to be taken according to his previous letter and for the administration to be submitted all the requested data in connection with the stealing of Golf cars. Did you see this letter and this reminder, or are you aware of its existence, Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know for a fact is that work on this was done continuously, but now when you ask me specifically about this document, I'm not quite sure. But I do know that work was being done on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, then can this document share the fate of the previous one, namely be MFI'd? I am not sure that conditions are ripe for it to be admitted into the case file, which is why I proposed this, or I can ask the witness to read it and to ask him whether he is familiar with its content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I say, I just -- sorry, you may have missed that, I have no objection to this being admitted. It's actually one of our documents, and we would have put it in if Mr. Cvijetic doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, so it could be marked -- admitted and marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit D183, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us just check.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 1D183.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I propose that we now take a look at document 1D94.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It is number 30, Mr. Borovcanin, in your binder. 1D94. Have you found it, Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you looked at it and you can see that the minister personally got involved in the investigation of this major case; do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please read the third paragraph of this document. There you can see that the minister is insisting for the centre of security services to immediately draw up a report on their previous work on this case and to make a progress report on it. I'm not quite sure whether you had occasion to see this document before. It has become an exhibit already, but you, I suppose, were aware of the minister's activities and its persistence in elucidating this case?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I know because many of the initiatives also came from the sessions of the Assembly of the Republika Srpska that were being held. And one of the deputies insisted on this issue being resolved, i.e., on the preventing of stealing Golf cars from the factory which manufactured them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Borovcanin, obstruction from Vogosca can be seen of the local authorities as well as of the public security station. How about you? Do you also see that there is obstruction there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the public security station of Vogosca was directly under our centre, and Unis or TAS was a major manufacturing firm which produced these Golf automobiles; it was in our area. So they should have been the first ones to actually respond to this dispatch and to submit intelligence and other information on its basis. Obviously, the inference to be drawn is that there was something wrong because they didn't do so, or that they were just withholding information because somebody among them was also involved in these shady deals.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the ministry had to clear -- clean its own house - when I say its own house, I'm referring to the specific station - and Mr. Maksimovic himself, when the inspector was there, also said that they used some vehicles for their own needs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the finding of one of the previous inspections, when he said to them that he had assigned some cars to the police officers. In that context, perhaps it will be interesting to say, I cannot prove it, but one of the locals offered to me, take one of these Golfs and have it registered anyway; you are in great danger; so when the war is over, we shall settle all these accounts. But I told him, Look, we are dealing in murky waters here; it is something that I wouldn't dream of doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us then look at document 65 ter 3096.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In your binder, Mr. Borovcanin, it is 31. So irrespective of the obstruction, both the ministry and your chief were persistent in seeking to elucidate this case. You see before you a ruling on measures of temporary removal from tasks and assignment, a suspension from work of precisely Mr. Borislav Maksimovic, because of a suspicion that he had committed a serious breach of work duty, had abused his office, and exceeded the bounds of his official authority. In paragraph 3 he is instructed to return his weapon and his official ID card. I'm now going to ask you to just explain, but please briefly, to the Trial Chamber, what is the essence of this measure of temporary suspension from work? But please be effective and please be brief.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, simply, the criminal offence which he had committed or was suspected of was sufficient reason for disciplinary proceedings to be instituted against him and for his weapons and ID card to be taken from him pending court procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So he was not longer able to continue working on his work post, his salary was diminished, and he was waiting for the outcome of the disciplinary proceedings; am I right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the period for completing disciplinary proceeding was, I believe, about six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Just tell me this, are you aware of this document about his temporary suspension and the institution of disciplinary proceedings against him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we went through these problems together.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You had the occasion to see this through the inspection controls?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, through the relevant service which actually did those controls.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move, Your Honours, that this be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the number. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I should repeat the number. 3096, according to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It's admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit 1D184, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, could you ask the witness, because this -- this document is -- doesn't say why Mr. Maksimovic is suspended disciplinary. Could you ask the witness if he knows if that is in relation with the TAS business?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have it two times. The following documents will speak about this, so that's when I was planning to ask him. Thank you. Could we now have the next document, please, 1D00-6682.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's tab 32 in your binder, Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please. Microphone for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: After the chief suspended Mr. Maksimovic, 15 days later there followed an unusual reaction from his policemen who opposed his being replaced and issued an ultimatum saying they would all abandon the public security station in Vogosca if the chief left, the chief appointed by the Assembly of Vogosca municipality, which alone had the authority to recall him. Mr. Borovcanin, we have a direct protest by the local police station and its a chief appointed by the local authorities. So this is in the context of what you said about it being difficult to establish the minister's authority in these local stations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: There's another interesting point in the original; it's signed by Mr. Maksimovic, although it has not been translated, the signature has not been translated, but it says Maksimovic in the Cyrillic alphabet. So he was very tenacious, wasn't he, at his local level; would you agree with that? Mr. Borovcanin, as the signature in the original is in Cyrillic, can you tell us who signed this? Can you read the signature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously it's Maksimovic's signature. It's quite legible, but let me add, we were not very surprised by this reaction because, metaphorically speaking, he had the wind in his sales because his policemen supported him since they themselves had taken part in those activities concerning the cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before -- just before it is tendered, could I ask Mr. Cvijetic, please, where the document comes from? Because it's not one of ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we took it from the disclosed material. We have it's ERN number. It's not our document. We took it from the materials disclosed to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: In any event, it's obviously a companion document to the last exhibit, so it's admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit 1D185, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, I will now show you the next document, 1D00-3711. It's 33 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right then. The situation was getting serious now. Someone had to be stronger. According to the minister's order, Mr. Borislav Maksimovic was arrested, two criminal reports against him were filed, and disciplinary proceedings were instituted. This document provides a summary of the criminal proceedings up to that point. In the fifth paragraph, it says that the proceedings were completed in 1993 and that Mr. Maksimovic's employment had been terminated as of the 16th of August, 1993, and he was placed at the disposal of the Army of the Republika Srpska. Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: If we go back to paragraph 2, we can see that in parallel with the disciplinary proceedings, two criminal reports against him were filed as a early as in November 1992. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In the context of what we said about the two separate proceedings, disciplinary and criminal, running in parallel, as well as his being put at the disposal of the army, his being placed at the disposal of the army did not obstruct either of the two proceedings, either disciplinary or criminal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That's how it was. So everything went on. Everything was done in the proper way. Of course, criminal proceedings may have been slow due to the lack of courts and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, we may now turn to the next page to answer His Honour's question as to what his criminal activities consisted in, and one can see this in the remaining part of the disciplinary proceedings. So please just look through this because it's quite long. So there are seven items containing descriptions of his criminal activities and misdemeanours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if we could look at the next several pages, please. It's the next page in English and in B/C/S as well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I will simply para-phrase, because I've read this, and you can check. The gist of the matter is very simple: People who had obtained Golf cars by theft, obtained certificates from Mr. Maksimovic saying that they were the true owners of the cars, and based on these certificates, they were able to register the cars at his police station and get licence plate numbers. Did you study this? Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So just a few of these activities would have been enough for him to be prosecuted, let alone all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The proceedings -- the disciplinary proceedings took quite a long time, probably the disciplinary organ had to wait for the criminal proceedings to be completed because under the law there is the presumption of innocence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have already mentioned that that was the rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But, however things may be, his employment in the Ministry of the Interior was terminated; that's what it says here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there's no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You know about these proceedings and you know about their outcome?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that we can now tender this important document which completes this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit 1D186, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I seem to have misnoted the date of document now 1D94, number 30 in the tab. Is that 1993, the date of the -- no, it's sorry, 31. The disciplinary ruling, 15 October 1993? Or 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you are referring to page 2, I think it's 1995, Your Honour. What page, sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The date of the ruling, the ruling -- the disciplinary ruling suspending Mr. Maksimovic. I think it's tab number 31, 65 ter 3096, if I'm not wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the 15th of October, 1992. That's the date that the decision was issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And can we then have the first page of the actual document, please, the document that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection. Just let me find it, please. Date is here as well, Your Honours. You can see it here in the description. It says that he was suspended as of the 15th of October, 1992, in the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Right. I was confused with 1, 2, 3, 4, the 5th paragraph where it's stated 16 August 1993, et cetera. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, what is the date of the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a summary, a recapitulation, of everything that was done in the case, so it contains all the dates of all the documents issued up to that point. And on the following page, you can see when the final decision was issued. The 16th of August, that's where the measure of termination of employment was handed down. And then Maksimovic appealed. The then-minister upheld the appeal and sent everything back for another proceeding, and then in 1995 his employment was terminated again. Is that clear now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I understand that the final decision to suspend Mr. Maksimovic was then reached on the 18th of September, 1995. Who is the author of this decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the decision on suspension. The suspension was handed down by Mr. Cvijetic. And throughout the disciplinary proceedings, he was suspended. But the decision on his disciplinary punishment was signed by the new chief, Milorad Maric, who was the minister at the time that decision was issued, because Mr. Cvijetic was killed and did not complete this case. That's on the last page of the final decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, although this has been admitted as an exhibit, you've described this as a summary. I'm wondering about the back documents which this summarises. Is there -- need we be apprehensive about being surprised somewhere down the line that the summary may have been inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can only assume that this was done by the office where the file was kept, and then the new chief, based on this summary, issued the new decision in 1995. And the document is mentioned up here, and we did show it to you, the document on suspension mentioned in the first line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. But my last comment was prompted by Ms. Korner's question three exhibits back as to what is the origin of this document. But, any way, we'll see; we'll see where we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, Mr. Maksimovic was not alone. Can you tell us what Mr. -- what post Mr. Kelovlankovic [as interpreted] had?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, Vlado was the commander of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then have 1D00-3697, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The first and last name was Vlado Kelovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So in parallel and at the same time as the chief, the criminal and disciplinary -- the same sort of criminal and disciplinary proceedings were also conducted against him. And, again, we have a summary of what was done in the case of Vlado Kelovic. And at the end we have an identical decision, and his employment was terminated because of the same violations concerning these cars. So we can just look at the next page, and we can see that a decision to terminate his employment was handed down?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He put to the witness that this was to do with the cars; where does it say that? Can I take it that a CJB is meant to be an SJB in the translation? Or was that a change in the ... But I'm more interested in where it says that this was all to do with the TAS thefts.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. We did that in the previous case. We have to go into the disciplinary proceedings documents and the decision on sanctions, and items 1, 2, 3, and 4 are lists of vehicles from the TAS factory that were the objective of this abuse. Read out item 1, 2, 3, and 4. We have to go page by page. Already in item 1 there is a reference to a VW Golf and its illegal registration. You can't see it in English because it's on page 2. It's all there now. Would that be sufficient now? Your Honours, to avoid asking the same questions again, I can just ask the witness if he is aware of these disciplinary proceedings against Mr. Kelovic and that they ended in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before the witness answers that question, if I may race ahead to the end of the road on which you seem to be headed with this document, having regard to the point that you were to establish in terms of the last series of questions with the previous document, does it assist dealing with this particular item? Is the Chamber -- will the Chamber be assisted by adding to the material the -- this item and the questions which you would wish to put to the witness arising from it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I indicated yesterday the lines of work and activities of the ministry in dealing with problems in various areas. I just announced that I would be talking about the line of questions concerning the engagement of the police in combat; then followed the line of questions concerning efforts to deal with the most serious crimes; and now I'm trying to see what kind of effect the minister's decisions and orders had, how they were carried out, and whether they had any effect on the work of the Ministry of the Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think I follow that. My only question was whether this advances anything. Proceed, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the same reasons as before, I would like to tender this document, and you will decide about its value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Did -- I interrupted you before the witness had answered the question that you were putting in respect to this document, so perhaps you have the witness's answer and then we'll decide whether we would accede to your application to have it tendered as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I have to repeat my question, Mr. Borovcanin. In your inspection work, did you have occasion to look at these disciplinary proceedings, whether they took place in keeping with the regulations, et cetera? Are you aware of this case?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. They went hand in hand, commander and chief. Because they were charged with abuse of official authority and position.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to add something. This goes to the Prosecution case in the part where they question whether anything was done about serious violations, what happened to the members of the MUP, who were responsible for such violations, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: By a majority, we agree that it should be -- that it may be admitted and marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit 1D187, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Since the witness said that Mr. Stanisic displayed persistence in dealing with problems in this area, I will finish this line of questioning with 1D73.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Did you mention the tab number to the witness, Mr. Cvijetic? It wasn't in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's tab 34. We need 1D73. It seems there's something wrong. I apologise, it's 1D173.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number 34 is 1D73.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's take the 65 ter number. It's 1936. It's a mistake, it's 173. We have a typo in our document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 173 is the right number. 1D173. That's the right document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's still under tab number 34?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it's tab 34 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We still don't have the English version. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You see on this list -- you see that this is the first meeting you probably don't know about held on the 20th December, 1992, it was convened by Mr. Radovan Karadzic; you see a list of people who were invited. And you see at the time Mico Stanisic was already the minister of the interior. Do you remember that, at this time, the government had resigned? I'll take you back because it seems there was no interpretation. This was an expanded meeting of the Supreme Command held on the 20th of December, 1992. You can see the composition. Mr. Stanisic was by that time already minister in the so-called -- in the so-called provisional government, and there was the prime minister designate because the governor had resigned. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember when Djeric resigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 3. It's page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Could you please focus on the contribution by Mr. Mico Stanisic. He is leaving the post, his ministerial post, and you will agree with me he is not satisfied with the progress hitherto in the affair of those scandals?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that this thing with the police station in Vogosca was just one operation which obviously had to continue and go deeper?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, it was just the tip of the iceberg, because what was mentioned in the disciplinary proceedings and the criminal prosecution concerning Mr. Maksimovic is the tip of the iceberg. A thousand Volkswagon Golfs were missing, and they were God knows where.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You must notice that Mr. Stanisic raised the issue of this scandal in the presence of the entire leadership, and he has the courage to persist, regardless of who might be involved?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you completely. And I can even add that I myself thought of this as a very courageous act for the time. And it's my personal opinion that the minister was beginning to irritate some people with his insistence. I can only tell you what I myself experienced when I said at one of the meetings to the political leadership, Gentlemen, please don't stand in the way of our work. Don't send scraps of paper saying that the recipient should be given a vehicle from the depot of seised cars. I thought that this was abuse of official authority. And this was leading nowhere. We could understand that vehicles could be requisitioned for official needs, but that they should be given to private persons without us knowing where the vehicle was going, this was crime. Thousands of such vehicles were driven away to all over Bosnia and Herzegovina and also -- not Croatia, I didn't mean to say Croatia. I meant to say Kiseljak, a Croat populated area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, we are at the point where we would ordinarily take the adjournment. Do I -- I gather that you have an hour and a half left, does that arithmetically mean that this witness will not be -- you will not have completed your cross-examination by the time we rise for the day at 1.45?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I will, if we take the break now. I will try to finish by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was assured that Mr. Cvijetic would finish by this adjournment. I cannot be here tomorrow, at the moment anyhow. Especially -- can I say, straightaway, I'm supposed to be going to a family funeral. I asked twice whether Mr. Cvijetic would finish by now as to allow Mr. Krgovic to ask, and I was assured that he would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And time for redirect.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And time for redirect. There would have been time if he'd finished now. Your Honours, of course, I mean, I accept that before I complain that Your Honours took a longer break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We will take the -- we will rise now and resume in 20 minutes. And maybe in the break counsel may consult and have some light shed on this when we return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If I -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Continuing with the matter of time that -- with which we were dealing when we took the adjournment, there is a possibility of us sitting an extra session this afternoon beginning at 2.15. I believe counsel may have been alerted to that. And we would -- if that is -- would be convenient, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very grateful for this. I wouldn't have mentioned what is ultimately a personal matter and should not affect the running of this trial. And if -- can I say, straightaway, if necessary, if it's not possible to sit an extra session, then, of course, I will make the arrangements accordingly. But if it can work, I'm very grateful to Your Honours, then it would help me enormously.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I offer my sincerest condolences to Ms. Korner over that family tragedy, and I want to say that I am prepared to accept any reasonable solution to deal with the problem that arose, if that means staying on this afternoon, it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Counsel for Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have any problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, as presently advised, there would be -- there's a possibility that this courtroom may be available, but if not, we would move to Courtroom III. So we would think in terms of resuming at 2.15 after the 1.45 break. Mr. Krgovic, how much time do you think that you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think half an hour probably because Mr. Cvijetic covered most of my topics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And Mr. Cvijetic, I believe that I may have misled you when I said that you have an hour and a half left; with think it's an hour. So with the time you have remaining and Mr. Krgovic and then re-examination, we should be able to complete this witness this afternoon. Mr. Borovcanin, we are taking steps to ensure that your testimony is completed by this afternoon. What it now appears to mean is that rather than taking the adjournment at the usual time at 1.45, we would be returning for another session beginning at 2.15. But the result would be that at the end of today's hearing, we would be in a position to release you. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, you still need to tell us to whom you addressed your complaint from the government, from the state leadership, telling them that they should leave you policemen to do your work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was a very important meeting attended by almost the entire leadership, including the prime minister designate, Mr. Branko Djeric; and across from me was sitting Momcilo Krajisnik, who, at the time, was the president of the Assembly. I addressed him directly asking him, and I will para-phrase the words I used then, Mr. President, please don't send us scraps of paper from Pale by way of certain people concerning these cars because it doesn't lead anywhere. And Mr. Djeric expressed his support for me during the break. He said he was glad to see there were policemen doing their job properly. So that we had the best intentions to have the minister's order complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 1D00-2420.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's tab 36 in your binder, Mr. Borovcanin. I hope you will recognise it, because it's from the Sarajevo CSB, and it's information about the crime prevention measures on the territory of the centre. And on page 1 you see statistical data; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So let's go through quickly. So let's look at the Milici SJB, and I'll tell you what we are dealing with now. We are dealing with war crimes. And it says here, three criminal reports were filed, or, rather, not filed because there is no prosecutor's office. I'm not sure we have touched on this problem, but I'm sure you observed it on the ground.
